examples.en: I watched the World Cup game on a live broadcast.
The live broadcast starts at six in the evening.
This channel broadcasts baseball games live.

examples.ko: 중계방송 해설자가 경기를 쉽게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The commentator on the broadcast explained the game in an easy way.
I was frustrated because the broadcast suddenly cut off.
They said a player's name wrong during the broadcast.

explain: 스포츠나 행사를 지금 벌어지는 대로 방송하는 것이에요. 줄여서 '중계'라고 하고, 녹화가 아니라 실시간이라는 점을 강조하면 '생중계'라고 해요. '중계방송을 하다', '중계방송을 보다', '중계방송을 듣다'로 써요.

phrases.en: Let's watch the game broadcast together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중계방송'의 줄임말이에요. 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of '중계방송', used more in speech.

phrases.en: I watched the opening ceremony live.
phrases.nuance_ko: 녹화가 아니라 실시간이라는 점을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses that it's real time, not recorded.

phrases.en: I listened to the radio broadcast in the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 라디오로 들을 때는 '듣다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '듣다' when listening on the radio.
phrases.en_equiv: to listen to a live broadcast

explain_en: It is broadcasting a sports match or event as it happens. It is shortened to 중계, and 생중계 stresses that it is real-time, not recorded. It appears as 중계방송을 하다, 중계방송을 보다, and 중계방송을 듣다.

t90.ax: This channel broadcasts baseball games live.

en: to be founded; to be established

examples.en: A new baseball team was founded in our city.
The choir was founded ten years ago.
A women's soccer team is scheduled to be founded next year.

examples.ko: 창단된 지 얼마 안 된 팀이라서 응원이 필요해요.
examples.en: It's a newly founded team, so it needs support.
I remember the day the orchestra was founded.

examples.ko: 학교에 응원단이 창단되고 나서 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The mood got better after a cheering squad was founded at school.

explain: 스포츠 팀, 합창단, 오케스트라처럼 '단'이 붙는 단체가 만들어질 때만 써요. 회사는 '설립되다', 학교는 '개교하다', 가게는 '문을 열다'라고 달라요.

phrases.example: 그 야구단은 창단된 지 오 년 됐어요.
phrases.en: That baseball team was founded five years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀이 생긴 지 얼마나 됐는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how long it has been since the team was founded.

phrases.en: A new orchestra is scheduled to be founded this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 생길 단체를 말할 때 '-ㄹ 예정이다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -ㄹ 예정이다 for a group that will be formed.

phrases.en: The choir's founding ceremony is being held tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단체가 처음 만들어졌음을 알리는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A ceremony announcing that the group has been formed.

explain_en: Use it only for groups ending in 단, such as sports teams, choirs, and orchestras. Companies are 설립되다, schools are 개교하다, and shops simply 문을 열다.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 황무지 개간에 힘을 모았어요.
examples.en: The villagers pooled their efforts to clear the wasteland.
Clearing a mountain slope is harder than you'd think.

examples.ko: 개간을 시작한 지 삼 년 만에 밭이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Three years after starting the land clearing, a field appeared.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 젊을 때 개간 일을 하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather did land-clearing work when he was young.

examples.ko: 무분별한 개간 때문에 숲이 줄어들고 있어요.
examples.en: Forests are shrinking because of reckless land clearing.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 개간이 끝나서 이제 농사를 지을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The clearing in this area is finished, so farming is now possible.

explain: 버려진 땅이나 숲을 갈아서 농사지을 수 있는 땅으로 만드는 일이에요. '개척'은 길이나 분야를 새로 연다는 더 넓은 말이라서, 땅을 농지로 바꾸는 경우에는 '개간'을 써요.

phrases.en: The government started a land reclamation project.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅을 농지로 만드는 공공 사업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a public project of turning land into farmland.

phrases.en: Clearing wasteland takes a lot of time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버려진 거친 땅을 쓸 수 있게 만드는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to making rough, abandoned land usable.

phrases.en: The villagers did the land clearing together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 땅을 만드는 일을 했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone actually did the work of clearing land.

explain_en: It is the work of turning abandoned land or forest into land that can be farmed. '개척' is broader, meaning opening up a new path or field, so for converting land into farmland you use '개간'.

examples.ko: 빛이 물을 지날 때 굴절이 일어나요.
examples.en: Refraction happens when light passes through water.

examples.ko: 컵 속 빨대가 꺾여 보이는 건 빛의 굴절 때문이에요.
examples.en: A straw in a cup looks bent because of the refraction of light.

examples.ko: 렌즈는 빛의 굴절을 이용해서 물체를 크게 보이게 해요.
examples.en: A lens uses the refraction of light to make objects look bigger.

examples.ko: 굴절 현상은 과학 시간에 실험으로 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned about the refraction phenomenon through an experiment in science class.
If the thickness of the glass differs, the refraction changes too.
I measured the angle of refraction with a protractor and recorded it.

explain: 빛이나 소리가 방향을 꺾는 현상을 말하는 과학 용어로 주로 써요. 거울에 부딪혀 돌아오는 '반사'와 구별해요. 사람의 마음이나 성격이 비뚤어졌다는 뜻으로 '굴절된 마음'이라고 쓰기도 하지만 글에서 보이는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: A rainbow forms because of the refraction of light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 수업에서 가장 흔하게 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in science classes.

phrases.en: Light is refracted when it enters water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이나 소리가 방향이 꺾일 때 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb form used when light or sound changes direction.

phrases.example: 물속 물건이 커 보이는 건 굴절 현상 때문이에요.
phrases.en: Objects looking bigger underwater is due to the refraction phenomenon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굴절이 일어나는 일 자체를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain the occurrence of refraction itself.

explain_en: It is mainly a science term for light or sound bending its direction. Do not confuse it with '반사' (reflection), where light bounces back from a mirror. It can also describe a twisted mind or personality, as in '굴절된 마음', but that is seen in writing.

examples.ko: 물을 끓이면 바닥에서 작은 기포가 올라와요.
examples.en: When you boil water, small bubbles rise from the bottom.

examples.ko: 반죽을 틀에 붓고 살살 두드려서 기포를 없애 주세요.
examples.en: Pour the batter into the pan and tap it gently to get rid of the air bubbles.

examples.ko: 컵 안쪽에 붙은 기포 때문에 물이 뿌옇게 보여요.
examples.en: The water looks cloudy because of the bubbles stuck to the inside of the cup.
The bubbles in sparkling water pop in your mouth.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 보호 필름에 기포가 생겨서 다시 붙였어요.
examples.en: Bubbles formed under the phone screen protector, so I put it on again.

examples.ko: 잠수부가 내뿜은 기포를 따라 작은 물고기들이 모였어요.
examples.en: Small fish gathered along the bubbles the diver let out.

explain: '거품'은 비누나 맥주처럼 여러 방울이 모여 덮인 것이고, '기포'는 물이나 액체 속의 공기 방울 하나하나를 가리킬 때 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '공기 방울'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 컵 안에 작은 공기 방울이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: Small air bubbles formed in the cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기포'를 일상 대화에서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say '기포'.

phrases.en: Bubbles keep forming in sparkling water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 액체 속에서 방울이 만들어지는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when bubbles appear in a liquid.

phrases.en: A small bubble popped in the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작은'을 앞에 붙여 방울의 크기를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting '작은' in front describes the size of the bubble.

explain_en: Single small bubble in liquid — technical, science, neutral. '거품' is a mass of bubbles covering a surface, like soap or beer foam, while '기포' fits better for individual air bubbles inside water or another liquid. In daily talk people also say '공기 방울'.

en: to swell; to roll; to heave

examples.ko: 태풍이 지나간 뒤 바다가 크게 너울졌어요.
examples.en: After the typhoon passed, the sea rolled with big swells.

examples.ko: 너울지는 파도 때문에 배가 많이 흔들려요.
examples.en: The boat rocks a lot because of the rolling swells.
The sea was swelling, so I couldn't fish.
Waves from far away come in as long swells.
They say the sea may swell today.
The clouds drift over the mountain in rolling waves.

explain: 바람이 불지 않아도 먼 바다의 영향으로 크고 길게 일렁이는 물결을 말할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '너울성 파도'라는 말로도 자주 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The heaving sea looked scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다를 꾸며 주는 말로, 큰 물결이 일렁이는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier for the sea, showing big waves rolling.

phrases.en: Waves swell widely out in the far sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금의 바다 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing the sea's state right now.

phrases.example: 바다가 계속 너울지고 있어서 배가 못 나가요.
phrases.en: The sea keeps swelling, so the boat can't go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물결이 계속 이어지는 상태를 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes that the swelling continues.

explain_en: Sea rolling in big swells, esp. before a storm. It describes big, long, rolling water that can appear even without wind, caused by conditions far out at sea. You may also hear it in the news as '너울성 파도' (swell waves).

en: to be buried; to be trapped

examples.en: A sudden landslide buried the road under soil.

examples.ko: 터널 안에 작업자 세 명이 매몰돼 있어요.
examples.en: Three workers are buried inside the tunnel.

examples.ko: 눈사태에 매몰된 사람을 구조대가 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: Rescuers are searching for the person buried in the avalanche.
The house almost got buried under the pile of earth.

examples.ko: 공사 중에 유물이 땅속에 매몰되어 있었어요.
examples.en: During construction, relics were found buried underground.

examples.ko: 일에 매몰되면 가족과 보낼 시간이 없어져요.
examples.en: If you get buried in work, you have no time for family.

explain: 흙이나 눈에 묻혀 보이지 않게 될 때 써요. 일이나 생각에 푹 파묻힌 상태를 비유할 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '묻히다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '매몰'은 사고 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The car was buried in the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easier word used more in daily life.

phrases.en: A burial accident happened on the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often heard in the news.

phrases.example: 요즘 일에 매몰돼서 쉴 시간이 없어요.
phrases.en: I'm buried in work these days and have no time to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일에 푹 파묻혀 있는 상태를 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative expression for being deeply immersed in work.

explain_en: Disaster/news — be buried by landslide, snow or collapse (눈에 매몰되다) It is used when something is covered by soil or snow and can't be seen. It can also describe being deeply sunk into work or thoughts. In daily talk '묻히다' is more common, while '매몰' is often heard in accident news.

dis.h: buried under earth or rubble, esp. disasters
gh: dead or deposits buried underground; formal

p.n: 묻히다 is plainer. 매몰되다 sounds like news reporting on a disaster.

t90.ax: Three workers are buried inside the tunnel.

examples.en: This region is famous as a top apple-growing area.
Jeju is a famous place of origin for tangerines.

examples.ko: 명산지에서 직접 가져온 배라서 맛이 달아요.
examples.en: These pears came straight from a famous growing area, so they taste sweet.
I heard that Icheon is a famous rice-producing area.
I planned a trip to tour famous tea-producing areas.
True to a famous producing area, every shop sells tangerines cheaply.

explain: 어떤 물건이 특히 잘 나기로 이름난 곳을 말해요. '사과 명산지'처럼 앞에 물건 이름을 붙여요. '특산물'은 그 지역의 물건을 가리키고, 명산지는 그 물건이 나는 장소를 가리킨다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: Boseong is known as a famous green tea producing area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 물건 이름을 붙여서 어떤 물건이 유명한 곳인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the product name before it to say what the place is famous for.

phrases.en: I went to a famous pear-growing area and bought some myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유명한 산지를 일부러 찾아간다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means going out of your way to visit a well-known producing area.
phrases.en_equiv: to visit a famous producing area

phrases.en: The specialty product of this region is pears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명산지는 장소, 특산물은 그곳에서 나는 물건을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A 명산지 is the place; a 특산물 is the product from there.

explain_en: It means a place famous for producing a particular product, with the product's name placed before it, as in '사과 명산지'. '특산물' refers to the regional product itself, while 명산지 refers to the place where it is produced.

examples.ko: 산에서 나무를 벌채하려면 허가를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: You need permission to fell trees on the mountain.

examples.ko: 무분별하게 벌채하면 산사태가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If trees are felled recklessly, landslides can happen.
The villagers cut down part of the forest.

examples.ko: 이곳은 벌채한 뒤에 새 나무를 심었어요.
examples.en: They planted new trees here after the logging.
The work of felling trees is dangerous.
You must not cut down trees without permission.

explain: '나무를 베다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 뉴스, 환경 이야기, 공문서에서 많이 나와요. 보통 숲이나 산에서 많은 나무를 베는 일에 써요. 집 마당의 나무 한 그루를 벨 때는 '베다'나 '자르다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The company felled the forest and built a road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌채하다'가 넓은 숲이나 산에 쓰이는 말이라는 걸 보여 주는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing; it shows 벌채하다 is used for large forests or mountains.

phrases.en: The people who felled trees illegally were caught.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 허가 없이 나무를 벨 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common news phrase for cutting trees without permission.

phrases.en: Logging is prohibited on this mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌채하다'를 '벌채'라는 명사로 바꿔 규칙이나 공고에서 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form 벌채 is used in rules and official notices.

explain_en: It is a more formal word than '나무를 베다', so it often appears in news, environmental topics and official documents. It usually refers to cutting down many trees in a forest or on a mountain. For a single tree in a yard, '베다' or '자르다' sounds more natural.

en: to spout; to gush out; to burst out

examples.en: Hot gas erupts from the volcano.
The discontent held in for so long burst out all at once.
There is a place where hot spring water gushes from the ground.
When magma erupts, the surroundings become dangerous.
The moment the emotion burst out, tears came.

examples.ko: 가스가 분출될 때 큰 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: A loud noise came when the gas was released.

explain: 물·불·가스·감정이 안에서 세게 밖으로 나올 때, 저절로 일어나는 일이면 '분출되다'를 써요. 사람이나 기계가 일부러 내보내면 '분출하다'예요. '불만이 분출되다'처럼 감정에도 써요.

phrases.en: Lava is erupting from the volcano.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화산 이야기에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in talk about volcanoes.

phrases.en: The sky grew dark because of the volcanic eruption.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사가 아니라 일어난 일을 명사로 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form, used to name the event itself.

phrases.en: The desires I had held back burst out all at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눌러 둔 마음이 갑자기 세게 나온다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for pent-up feelings suddenly bursting out.

explain_en: Passive — something bursts out by itself, as with volcanoes (연기가 분출되다) When water, fire, gas or emotion comes forcefully out from inside, and it happens by itself, use 분출되다. When a person or machine sends it out on purpose, use 분출하다. It also works for feelings, as in '불만이 분출되다'.

t90.ax: Hot gas erupts from the volcano.

examples.en: Baekdudaegan is the great mountain range running across the Korean Peninsula.
The mountain range stretches long to the east.
A hiking trail continues along the ridge line.

examples.ko: 두 산줄기 사이에 깊은 계곡이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a deep valley between the two mountain ranges.
This village is surrounded by mountain ridges.
The weather is a little different in each mountain range.

explain: 여러 산이 줄처럼 길게 이어진 모양을 말해요. 학교 지리나 과학에서는 '산맥'이라는 말을 쓰고, '산줄기'는 이어진 산의 흐름을 말할 때 자연스러워요. 지도 설명이나 등산 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 태백산맥은 동쪽에 길게 뻗어 있는 산맥이에요.
phrases.en: The Taebaek Mountains are a long range stretching along the east.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지리 수업이나 지도에서 쓰는 이름이고, '산줄기'보다 공식적인 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The term used in geography and on maps, more formal than '산줄기'.

phrases.en: I walked for several days along the mountain ridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이어진 산의 흐름을 따라 이동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving along a chain of connected mountains.

phrases.en: A big mountain range continues to the north.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산이 줄처럼 계속 연결된 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes mountains connecting in a continuous line.

explain_en: Mountain line seen stretching on and on, as from a plane. It describes many mountains connected in a long line. In school geography the term '산맥' is used, while '산줄기' sounds natural when talking about the flow of connected mountains. It often appears in map descriptions and hiking talk.

t90.ax: The mountain range stretches long to the east.

en: in a heap; piled up softly

examples.en: Snow piled up softly and the road turned white.
She heaped rice onto my plate.
Fallen leaves piled up in the flower bed.
Dust has settled thickly on the desk.

examples.ko: 할머니가 그릇에 쌀을 소복이 퍼 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother scooped a heaping bowl of rice for me.

examples.ko: 아이가 모래를 소복이 모아 산을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child gathered sand into a little mound to make a mountain.

explain: 눈, 낙엽, 밥, 먼지처럼 무언가가 둥글게 볼록 쌓이거나 담긴 모습에 써요. '수북이'와 비슷하게 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 보통 '쌓이다, 담다, 앉다'와 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: Fruit is piled high on the plate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소복이'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 양이 더 많고 높게 쌓인 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 소복이, but suggests a larger, higher pile.

phrases.example: 소복이 쌓인 눈 위를 천천히 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I walked slowly over the snow that had piled up softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌓인'을 붙여 눈이 둥글게 쌓인 풍경을 말할 때 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '쌓인', it describes a snowy scene where snow has gathered in a soft mound.

phrases.en: I filled the bowl with a heap of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 볼록하게 가득 담을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for heaping food into a dish.

explain_en: It describes things such as snow, leaves, rice or dust piled up or filled in a rounded heap. It is often used much like '수북이'. It usually appears with verbs like '쌓이다', '담다' and '앉다'.

en: to be swept; to be swept away

examples.en: The fallen leaves were swept by the wind and gathered on one side.

examples.ko: 파도에 쓸려 온 쓰레기가 해변에 가득해요.
examples.en: The beach is full of trash washed in by the waves.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 흙이 다 쓸려 내려갔어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so all the soil was washed away.
My heel hurts because the new shoes rubbed it raw.

examples.ko: 물살에 쓸리지 않게 제 손을 꼭 잡으세요.
examples.en: Hold my hand tightly so you aren't swept away by the current.

examples.ko: 눈이 깨끗이 쓸린 길로 천천히 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly along the road where the snow had been swept clean.

explain: '쓸다'의 피동으로, 바람이나 물에 밀려가는 것 또는 살갗이 스쳐 아픈 것에 써요. 감정이나 분위기에 끌려가는 것은 '휩쓸리다'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The umbrella was swept away by the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이나 물에 밀려서 멀리 가 버릴 때 '쓸려 가다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something is pushed far away by wind or water.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 흙이 쓸려 내려갔어요.
phrases.en: It rained a lot, so the soil was washed down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에 밀려 아래로 내려갈 때 써요. 비, 강, 홍수 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is carried downward by water; common with rain, rivers, and floods.

phrases.example: 넘어질 때 무릎이 바닥에 쓸려서 아파요.
phrases.en: My knee scraped on the ground when I fell, and now it hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살갗이 스쳐서 아플 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for skin that hurts from being rubbed.

explain_en: This is the passive of '쓸다', used for things pushed along by wind or water, or skin that gets scraped. For being carried away by emotion or the mood, people often say '휩쓸리다' instead.

examples.en: My hands are as cold as ice.

examples.ko: 방바닥이 얼음장 같아서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The floor was ice cold, so I couldn't sleep.
The sheet of ice on the lake is thin, so it's dangerous.

examples.ko: 겨울 바다에서는 얼음장 같은 바람이 불어요.
examples.en: An icy wind blows at the winter sea.

examples.ko: 그의 얼음장 같은 표정에 분위기가 싸늘해졌어요.
examples.en: His icy expression made the atmosphere chilly.
The boiler broke, so the house is freezing.

explain: 실제 얼음판도 뜻하지만, '얼음장 같다/얼음장처럼'으로 손, 방바닥, 물, 표정이 아주 차가울 때 비유로 많이 써요. 반대로 열이 심하게 나는 몸에는 '불덩이 같다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I put my hand in water as cold as ice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '같은'을 붙여 아주 찬 것을 꾸미는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 같은 it describes something extremely cold.

phrases.en: I held his ice-cold hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손이나 몸이 차가울 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when hands or the body are very cold.

phrases.en: Walk carefully on the sheet of ice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유가 아니라 실제 얼음판을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it means actual ice, not a comparison.

explain_en: It can mean an actual sheet of ice, but it is often used as a comparison, '얼음장 같다' or '얼음장처럼', for very cold hands, floors, water or even expressions. For a body with a high fever, the opposite image is '불덩이 같다'.

en: to melt; to dissolve; to go into solution

examples.ko: 설탕은 뜨거운 물에 더 빨리 용해돼요.
examples.en: Sugar dissolves faster in hot water.

examples.ko: 소금이 물에 완전히 용해될 때까지 저어 주세요.
examples.en: Please stir until the salt has completely dissolved in the water.

examples.ko: 이 약은 물에 용해되지 않아서 그냥 삼켜야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine doesn't dissolve in water, so you have to swallow it as is.

examples.ko: 비타민 가루가 물에 용해되면 색이 조금 변해요.
examples.en: When the vitamin powder dissolves in water, the color changes a little.
Check whether the powder has all dissolved.

examples.ko: 알약이 물에 용해되는 속도는 제품마다 달라요.
examples.en: The speed at which a tablet dissolves in water differs by product.

explain: '녹다'와 비슷하지만 설탕이나 소금이 물에 섞여 녹는 것처럼 과학 수업이나 설명서에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '녹다'라고 해요. 보통 '물에 용해되다'처럼 '~에' 앞에 녹이는 액체를 써요.

phrases.example: 비타민 가루가 물에 용해되면 마셔도 돼요.
phrases.en: Once the vitamin powder dissolves in water, you can drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용해되다'는 보통 이렇게 녹이는 액체를 '~에' 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 용해되다 usually puts the liquid that does the dissolving before '~에,' like this.

phrases.example: 컵에 설탕을 넣고 물에 용해시켜 보세요.
phrases.en: Put sugar in the cup and try dissolving it in water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용해되다'와 달리 사람이 일부러 녹게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 용해되다, it means a person deliberately makes something dissolve.

phrases.en: Sugar dissolves quickly in warm tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용해되다'와 같은 뜻을 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the everyday way to say the same thing as 용해되다.

explain_en: Formal, scientific; substance dissolves in liquid. It is close to '녹다' but is a stiffer word used in science classes and instructions, for example sugar or salt mixing into water. In daily conversation people just say '녹다'. It usually takes the liquid with '~에', as in '물에 용해되다'.

t90.ax: Sugar dissolves faster in hot water.
